accepted.sentence: Typically elongated and gently curved, this fruit has a thick peel surrounding pale, soft flesh.
Its peel is green when unripe and commonly turns yellow as the flesh ripens.
Ripening converts much of its starchy flesh into sugars, making the taste sweeter and texture softer.
The edible interior contains substantial water alongside carbohydrates, especially starch in less-ripe specimens.
Cultivated dessert varieties usually have tiny, undeveloped seeds rather than large, hard seeds.
The outer skin contains fibrous tissues that help protect the easily bruised interior.
Its flesh supplies potassium and also contains vitamin B6 and vitamin C.
A ripe interior is creamy and tender, while the peel remains tougher and more elastic.
